title: An explicit counterexample to three-summand Kato-kernel splitting
version_source: native metadata.version; no numeric version printed in PDF
original_abstract: Question 2 in Laghribi’s contribution to Oberwolfach Report 5/2016 asks whether a mixed Kato kernel is the sum of the kernels of a finite purely inseparable extension, a separable quadratic extension, and a bilinear Pfister function field. We give an explicit negative instance in H₂², using an exponent-two extension and a binary bilinear Pfister form that remains anisotropic. The mixed class is exactly a specialization of the generators of Aravire–Laghribi–O’Ryan (2019/2020). We prove directly that it remains outside the sum after the additional Pfister kernel is included, by a universal norm and residue obstruction. The original degree-one cohomology case is separately positive. No firstness claim is made.
description: An exponent-two characteristic-two example disproves three-summand Kato-kernel splitting at n=1; the n=0 boundary remains positive.
rights: Authored paper, code and analysis CC BY 4.0; third-party rights retained
positive_boundary: Original n=0 equality for all stated positive-fold data
function_field_convention: projective quasilinear quadric, includes integral zero-dimensional binary case
mixed_generator_credit: Aravire–Laghribi–O’Ryan2019/2020; direct survival argument after third kernel added
